sentence: This project builds computational models of massive stars that explode as supernovae, to predict the light those explosions produce.
This project designs brush-like polymer networks to make adhesives that need no additives and can be switched on demand.
This project tests whether more nutrients in the oceans led to the spread of eukaryotes, organisms with nuclei in their cells.
This project studies how soybean seeds keep their protein and amino acid content steady when one seed storage protein is reduced.
This project studies dark energy, dark matter, black holes and how stars and galaxies change, using machine learning on theoretical and observational datasets.
This project develops statistical methods and artificial intelligence tools to look for signs of physics beyond the Standard Model in particle physics data.
This project studies how hard it is to learn, estimate and simulate the collective behaviour of interacting quantum particles using computers.
This project studies how reservoirs can be run using weather forecasts to balance water supplies, flood risks and ecological needs.
This project combines RNA sequencing methods with machine learning to predict how much protein a cell makes from an mRNA.
This project studies whether pulsed electric fields can change how easily things pass through the cells lining blood vessels, to help drugs reach tumors.
This project builds light-based sensors from metal nanostructures that detect disease markers such as nucleic acids and proteins in blood and urine samples.
This project builds biochemical reaction networks that produce repeated oscillations in small droplets and studies how they behave in cell-like systems.
This project builds a statistical theory that explains how large language models work with prompting methods such as in-context learning and chain-of-thought prompting.
This project studies figs, the small wasps that pollinate them and parasitic wasps, to find out how their interactions change and evolve.
This project studies molecular ions with electron-deficient nitrogen atoms to learn how to stabilize them while keeping their electronic and magnetic properties.
This project builds graph neural networks that help robots predict how sand or soil responds when they dig, using camera images and sensed forces.
This project compares heavy-ion collision experiments with simulations, using machine learning and Bayesian analysis, to learn how dense and hot nuclear matter behaves.
